To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrogels can stabilize soil structure by gluing soil particles together and that the degree of structural stabilization is directly related to the amount of water bound to the hydrogel.

the swelling and shrinkage of a hydrogel can be detected by NMR relaxometry, and that the structural stability of the soil is affected by the swelling and shrink processes of the incorporated hydrogel.
hydrogel induced soil stabilization can only be achieved if a hydrogel is exposed to moisture dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of soil organic matter on soil structural stability and its implications for soil functioning.
the development of a new methodology for the investigation of soil structural stability.
the impact of soil organic matter (OM) on soil structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the swelling of the hydrogel is a key factor for structural stabilization.
the swelling/shrinking processes of the incorporated hydrogels are responsible for the dynamic and hysteretic nature of the soil structural stabilization.
the hydrogel induced soil stability is not only related to the swelling capacity of the hydrogel, but also to the water dynamics within the hydrogel and the pore space of the soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the swelling and shrinking of the incorporated hydrogel in the soil is a major factor for the development of structural stability in a soil with insufficient clay content.
the incorporation of a hydrogel forming substance can stabilize the soil structure in an unstable, silty soil.
the combination of NMR relaxometry with rheology can be used to understand the development of SOM associated water and its role for structural stability in dependence of environmental changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hydrogel forming organic substances can enhance the stability of unstable, sandy soils, which is of great importance in the context of soil erosion and land degradation.
hydrogel induced soil stabilization is a dynamic process which is affected by the soil moisture dynamics.
hydrogel induced structural stability is not only a function of soil water content but rather a function of water dynamics.
